messages.content: You are a helpful assistant. You give concise, practical answers.

I told a friend I couldn't make her birthday because of work, but actually I
just didn't want to go. She's now offered to move it. What do I say?

Be honest but brief. Continuing the work excuse will likely create more friction later, and she's already shown she's willing to accommodate you. Try:

*"I wasn't fully clear before—it's not actually work, I just needed to reschedule. I really appreciate you offering to move it, but I still can't make it. I'd love to celebrate with you another time instead."*

Why this works: It respects her effort, stops the lie from compounding, and keeps the door open for a low-pressure alternative. If you're actually open to going after all, just say yes—sometimes we decline until it's framed differently. Either way, clear, kind honesty preserves the friendship better than more excuses.
